concept: One path for the heat. A single server's heat is followed outward, from the chip to the outside of the building, along one route the camera travels (right is outward along the path, down is inside a part, a zoom enters a thing). Air and coolant are moving streams and beads coloured cool and warm, the same in the 2D sections and in the 3D models, and the route promised at the start (b03) is lit stage by stage at the close (b30 to b32), around the same one server the film opens on.

story.metaphor: none: the real path the heat takes, from the chip to the outside of the building
story.setting: One invented, generic data centre (no site, no vendor): a server, a hall, the room from above, one rack, one AI server and its chip, the CDU and the outside, drawn as clean 2D sections, and as 3D models where seeing the object itself is the point
story.arc: Hook: one server's heat, then a room of them, and the question where it goes. Setup: the air path, server to cooling unit to outside. Turn: the goal is not a cold room, it is a path. Reveal: the room from above, aisles, the leak through an empty slot, the panel and containment. Turn: AI racks need liquid. Reveal: chip, cold plate, CDU and its two loops. Data: PUE as energy objects. Payoff: the opening server with the whole path lit, and the rule.

devices.what: The heat path map (kit heat_route): the chip to the outside as one route. A faint dashed promise at the start, the air path lit as one continuous line when the misconception breaks, and both lanes (liquid above, air below) lit stage by stage at the close. Every stage is a small object with its word on it.

One floor plan from above, held while one thing changes per run: every row the same way, the prediction on the plan, the row-to-row exhaust, the rotation into cold and hot aisles; then a zoom into one aisle, in 3D.

Air and coolant drawn as moving streams or beads, cool in accent4 and warm in accent2, identical in the 2D sections and the 3D models. A stream recolours where it picks up or gives off heat, so the viewer watches the heat travel.

One rack returns, changed each time: the empty slot (3D), its side section with the leak, the blanking panel sliding in (3D), the same slot seen from the aisle, then filled with AI servers and a flood of heat, and as a small callback card beside the liquid-cooled server.

Energy as objects, never a headline number: beads poured into an IT bin and overhead bins (physics), then blocks stacked as the PUE fraction that holds while the overhead shrinks, returns and grows with the leaks. The only number ever printed is 1.0.

The join material: the camera travels with the heat. Right is outward along the path, up is a pull back to the room, down is inside a part, and a zoom enters a thing (the plan into one aisle, the CDU into its two loops). Section changes are hard cuts.

A flood at the turn: AI servers arrive and warm colour floods the back of the rack, the only time amber covers a large area.
Colour withheld for the hardest idea: inside the CDU everything is neutral except the two loops and the heat crossing between them.

parts.what: The heat path map as a long horizontal strip. Left end: one server in cutaway (the server_side part, small) with its chip. Right end: the building's outer wall and one generic outdoor unit releasing warm air to open air. Two lanes run between them: the upper, liquid lane (chip, cold plate, rack loop, CDU, facility water, outside) and the lower, air lane (front, back, hot aisle, cooling unit, then a water line to the same outdoor unit). Each stage is a small neutral object with its label hung on it (28 px or larger). A lane segment is faint (dashed, line token), lit (temperature colours: accent4 before the heat is picked up, accent2 after) or named (accent, while the narration names it).

One server in side view: a flat chassis with fans at the front on the left (intake) and the back on the right (exhaust), a chip under a heatsink in the middle, memory and power supplies beside it. Air form: a cool stream (accent4) enters the front and turns warm (accent2) as it crosses the hot parts, leaving the back. Liquid form: a cold plate on the chip with a cool hose in and a warm hose out of the back, and a thinner air stream still crossing the other parts.

The room from above: walls, a raised-floor tile grid (surface2), two cooling units on the bottom wall, four rows of racks as long ink bars of six rack tiles each, numbered 1 to 4 from the bottom (the front row, nearest the cooling units) to the top (the back row). Each row's front edge carries a small arrow. same_way: every front points down. alternating: rows 1 and 3 turned round in place, so fronts face across a cold aisle between rows 1 and 2 and between rows 3 and 4, backs across a hot aisle between rows 2 and 3; aisle washes (cold accent4, hot accent2 at low opacity) with labels. Rows 1 and 2 and the cold aisle between them sit inside x 640 to 1280, y 520 to 880 of the frame, so the b12 zoom lands on them.

One rack of servers, two views. Side section: the frame with its front (cold aisle side, left) and back (hot aisle side, right), seven servers stacked with one empty slot third from the top, cool intake streams on the left, warm exhaust on the right. Front view (seen from the aisle): the same rack face-on, the same empty slot, a perforated floor tile in front. gap: the slot open. blanked: a blanking panel fills it. ai: every server swapped for a taller AI server whose accelerator blocks glow warm, the exhaust band several times wider.

PUE as a fraction of energy blocks: a top stack (IT energy blocks in accent3 at its base, overhead blocks in line grey above them, the cooling block the largest of the overhead), a fraction bar, a bottom stack (the same IT energy blocks), the labels Total facility energy (top) and IT energy (bottom), and a thin floor line where the top would equal the bottom. built; ideal (no overhead, top equals bottom); real (a little overhead back, the top just above the floor line); grown (one more overhead block).

kit.notes: Colours: cool accent4, warm accent2 everywhere (the 3D models use the same tokens); accent (blue) only on the element being named, one at a time; context in accent3, line and muted. Every label 28 px or larger as seen, words only from the script or the knowledge sheet. No people anywhere (the brief: no presenter; the floor team is never drawn).

scenes.subject: two separate loops passing heat across a heat exchanger

design.treatment: Inside the CDU as a clean schematic (no cabinet detail). A heat exchanger in the centre, a stack of thin neutral plates. The rack loop on the left: a closed pipe loop running out to the left edge toward the racks. The facility water loop on the right: its own closed loop running out to the right edge toward the building. Beads move round each loop: the rack loop arrives warm (accent2) and leaves the exchanger cool (accent4); the facility loop arrives cool and leaves warm. Small warm chevrons cross the plates from left to right. A strip of plain field runs down the middle of the exchanger between the two loops: they never touch. The accent moves to whatever is being named.
design.why_motion: The hardest idea of the film: heat crosses while each liquid stays in its own loop. Only motion shows both at once.

scenes.subject: energy pouring into IT and overhead bins
scenes.upgrade_reason: Overhead is energy that goes somewhere other than computing: watching one stream split into bins, cooling the fullest of the overhead, says it without a number; a template would need a figure the knowledge sheet does not carry.

design.treatment: Energy as objects, physically (Loom.physics.puePour): a feed pipe at the top labelled Total facility energy pours energy beads that split into an IT energy bin and three overhead bins (Cooling, Power losses, Lighting; the names are from the knowledge sheet). A bracket groups the overhead bins, labelled Overhead. The Cooling bin is clearly the fullest of the overhead bins and its label takes the accent on its word. The bead counts are a picture of the claim (cooling is the biggest slice of the overhead), not a measurement: print no counts, no shares and no ratio (showShares false, no ratioText). Sketch of opts: itShare 0.62, overheads [[Cooling, 0.26], [Power losses, 0.08], [Lighting, 0.04]], beads 28, colors {it: accent3, overhead: line, bead: muted}, t on the first anchor, seconds about 4.5.
design.why_motion: Energy splitting as it pours is the point: it is one flow, and part of it never reaches the computing.
